glossary.description: The marketing channel a campaign runs on: search, social, display, email or partner. Leads and bookings take their campaign's channel; a booking whose lead is not loaded yet has none.

A lead that books. Bookings count conversions on the day they are made; the lead-to-booking rate counts a lead as converted when it books within 30 days of being created; cost per conversion is cost per booking.
The customer's ISO-2 country. It is not the market a campaign targets nor a lead's country, so revenue or orders by country group by it.

A customer with any site or CRM action (a page view, a cart, a checkout, an email opened, a support contact) in the trailing window ending on the day: 7 days for weekly, 28 for monthly. It is not an active customer, which counts customers who placed a non-cancelled order.
A partner at least one of whose contacts replied to an outreach message in the period asked. A reply to a message sent before the first loaded day counts as a reply but names no partner.

Where a candidate is in hiring: applied, screen, interview, offer, then hired, or rejected at any stage before hired. A candidate's stage on a day is the one they were in at the end of that day, from the stage history the warehouse snapshots after every load, so two changes between loads keep the later.
The ISO-2 country a campaign targets. It can differ from a lead's own country and a customer's country, so spend, leads and bookings by market group by the campaign, not the person.
Where an order stands: placed, shipped or cancelled. A cancelled order counts in orders and the cancellation rate, never in revenue or active customers.
An order a partner reports as returned, with the amount and the partner's reason, on the UTC day it was recorded. Returns lower net revenue; revenue itself keeps the order.
The customers who signed up in the same calendar month. A metric by cohort groups by the month its customer signed up, not the month the order was placed.

The steps a site session walks: page view, then add to cart, then checkout. A step's rate counts the sessions that took the next step on the same day as the step before or the day after, on the day of the step before.
